pill.desc: clear, colorless liquid in a single-dose vial

tell: A recombinant erythropoietin that also carries an indication to reduce red cell transfusions in elective, noncardiac surgery.

clues.text: Pharmacokinetics in pediatric patients resemble those in adults, with no apparent difference in patients above or below 65 years of age.
A 165-amino acid recombinant molecule made in mammalian cells, with a molecular weight of about 30,400 daltons.
Approved under BLA 103234 as single-dose vials of 2,000 to 10,000 Units/mL and multiple-dose vials of 20,000 Units/2 mL.
Boxed warning for death, heart attack, stroke, clots and tumor progression. Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension, pure red cell aplasia and serious allergic reactions.
Anemia from chronic kidney disease in patients on or off dialysis, from zidovudine in HIV, and from chemotherapy; also reducing transfusions in some surgery.
Stimulates red cell production by the same mechanism as the body's own erythropoietin.
The generic name begins with E and has two words and eleven letters.
